digest.component_or_area: reconciler `.bridge_state` committed cache and tickets-store growth mitigation
propositions: The reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache causes 92% (1.04 GiB) of tickets-store growth; 18 MB bindings.json grows 12.79 KB per committed revision due to timestamp and rotation bookkeeping fields that are unused or read nowhere in src/.

Deleting the `baseline_advanced_at` timestamp reduces marginal cost 7.4x to 1.74 KB per version; moving `last_get_pass` rotation bookkeeping to a separate sidecar file halves version count for 12.8x total reduction.

The cache must remain on-branch and committed because the reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners; the fix optimizes content and churn, not location, via write-when-changed guards and field normalization.

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/fast-import reduces existing history from 1.17 GiB to 98.8 MB (8.4%), preserves all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges, and maintains byte-identical HEAD tree after dynamic re-add.

Rollout gates include descendant workflow execution, explicit host refresh, live epoch-mismatch refusal probes, and a short quiesced publication window with off-repo backup bundle verification and operator attestation of zero sessions and stopped rebar-mcp processes.

Post-publish rollback is a second quiesced window using direct ref replacement with operator oversight; new-epoch clones must be replaced to preserve fail-closed epoch-mismatch safety without application-level union bypass.
